mapping.old: An exact finite counterexample can falsify a universal inequality. Finite computation can also locate dangerous faces and expose candidate exact identities; it cannot prove cofinal no-escape, all-order positivity, common-zero landing, or RH.
mapping.new: A single exact counterexample can disprove a proposed universal inequality. A finite successful scan cannot establish Riemann hypothesis (RH), positivity at every matrix size, escape control as a cutoff tends to infinity, or a common-zero theorem. Use successful scans to select the next statement to prove, not as that proof.

mapping.old: Positive signs from floating-point scans remain conjectural. Near clustered atoms, high Hankel rank, large theta action, or tiny Galerkin energies, low precision routinely creates false negative eigenvalues/signs.
mapping.new: [Observation] Numerical sign tests are especially unreliable when spectral points nearly coincide, moment matrices have high rank, or an exponentially small signal is obtained by subtracting large terms. Increasing precision has repeatedly removed apparent negative eigenvalues. A small computed eigenvalue needs a conditioning and precision check before it can reject a mechanism.

mapping.old: Exact algebra discovered numerically is usable only after independent symbolic proof. Several such survivors below are now Lean-checked.
mapping.new: [Research rule] An exact-looking identity suggested by computation becomes an analytic result only after an independent derivation. Some entries below report such derivations; none licenses importing a saved numerical coefficient table as a premise in Lean.

mapping.old: Repeated lesson: scalar, diagonal, pointwise, fixed-block, or fixed-order control usually deletes the mixed cancellation carrying the actual source.
mapping.new: [Interpretation] Many failed shortcuts kept only diagonal terms, one scalar component, pointwise signs, or a fixed matrix size. The surviving arithmetic expressions often rely on cancellation between the omitted components. Before strengthening a bound, check whether the quantity being bounded still contains the source's mixed terms.

mapping.old: `[observed]` Literal completed-theta C5 stayed nonnegative on all tested domains; its only observed tight limit is coalescence `t→0`, with margin of order `t⁴`. The safe mechanism is cumulative compensation in the hard negative-elasticity chamber, not nonnegative elasticity.
mapping.new: [Observation] The fifth-root curvature inequality for the literal completed-theta source, called C5, was nonnegative at all tested admissible points. Its smallest margins occurred when the two reflected evaluation points coalesced; the margin then scaled as the fourth power of their separation. The tested source lay in the negative-elasticity region, so positivity must come from the combined balance, not from assuming elasticity is nonnegative.

mapping.old: `[observed]` Completed-theta Bezoutian sections were positive through rank 20 after precision escalation; tiny high-rank eigenvalues reflect analytic-kernel conditioning, not detected sign failure.
mapping.new: [Observation] Finite sections of the completed-theta Bezoutian kernel were positive through matrix rank 20 after increasing precision. This supports further investigation of that specific kernel. It does not establish positivity at arbitrary rank; the very small eigenvalues make extrapolation particularly unsafe.

mapping.old: `[observed/rejected]` Numerics found no total-positivity violation through order 4 and a robust failure at order 5. Rank-≤4 C5 structure lies inside the observed free TP range; no `TP_m` mechanism with `m≥5` can close higher packets.
mapping.new: [Observation; rejected extension] The tested completed-theta kernel had no detected total-positivity violation through order four, but a stable violation occurred at order five. Here total positivity means nonnegativity of all ordered minors of the specified order. An argument requiring this kernel to be totally positive at every order, or at order five and above, cannot be justified by its successful low-order tests.

mapping.old: `[observed]` Li coefficients stayed positive through degree 300; shifted zero-moment Hankel and support-side matrices stayed positive through size 12. High precision is mandatory because atom clustering creates false negative signs.
mapping.new: [Observation] The tested Li coefficients were positive through degree 300, and the tested moment/support matrices built from zeta-zero data were positive through size 12. These are finite checks of positivity conditions related to RH. Clustered zero data made low-precision moment matrices produce false negative signs; neither successful range proves the infinite sequence of inequalities.

mapping.old: `[rejected]` Endpoint-ratio confinement, local log-concavity, Riccati positivity, and positive finite theta-atom mixing do not imply C5: admissible 2–4 atom mixtures give negative balance. Exact modular coefficient coupling is essential.
mapping.new: [Rejected mechanism] Positivity of theta-shaped atoms, local log-concavity, endpoint-ratio bounds and the tested Riccati inequality do not together force the C5 curvature inequality. Positive mixtures of only two to four admissible atoms violate it. A proof for the literal theta source therefore needs its particular coefficient relations, or another constraint absent from those mixtures.

mapping.old: `[observed]` At fixed action, the direct transverse C5 Jacobian stayed positive. Reflection gives exact seam zero; the correct target is the desingularized sign `J(u,t)/u`, not the raw Jacobian at `u=0`.
mapping.new: [Observation] For the C5 balance F and reflected log action q, the fixed-action Jacobian J=F_u q_t−F_t q_u was positive in the tested interior. Reflection forces J=0 at the symmetry center u=0. The useful boundary target is therefore the limiting sign of J/u, not strict positivity of J at the symmetry center.

mapping.old: `[proved]` First-atom base compensation is positive on the same half-line. Its seam margin first appears at order `t⁷` with an explicitly shifted-positive degree-7 polynomial. Termwise sign of the intermediate `P₂` polynomial is false.

mapping.old: `[observed]` Modular-center C5 velocity stayed strictly positive from seam to far cusp; no stationary point was detected. Direct radial monotonicity is a stronger surviving target than stationary-locus reserve accounting.

A possible sufficient route is M'''(lambda)>0, M''(0)>=0 and M'(0)>=−M(0)/5, with M(0)>0 and 0<=lambda<=1. mapping.old: `[rejected]` Even fixed mass, support gap, conditional first moment, and positive lower-transport curvature do not force the enlarged-source compensation inequality: a remote escaping atom makes compensation negative while preserving those data. mapping.old: `[rejected]` Scalar center-independent damped Fourier corrections have incompatible required signs at different centers for tested dampings. Sufficiently fast damping fails analytically because its correction vanishes inside the formally negative native rank-three chamber; sufficiently slow damping also cannot close the zero-mass proposal. A full center-frequency flux still needs the signed positive-vs-negative mass comparison.
mapping.new: [Rejected mechanism] A single center-independent, damped Fourier correction cannot repair the tested reflected-theta determinant at all centers: different centers require incompatible correction signs. Fast damping also makes the correction disappear inside a known negative rank-three region, while slow damping fails the proposed zero-mass construction. Any surviving correction needs coupled center/frequency information and a bound on the complete signed mass balance.

mapping.old: `[observed]` A fixed canonical even correction and both endpoints of its coefficient band stayed positive on the tested middle interval, including complete entry/correction error majorants. Uniform signed interval control remains open.
mapping.new: [Observation] One fixed even Fourier correction, including both endpoints of its allowed coefficient interval, kept the tested middle-region determinant positive after the stated entry and correction error allowances. This supports that specific compact-region construction. Uniform interval control of the signed errors remains open; sampled corrected positivity is not a certificate for the whole region.

mapping.old: `[proved]` Exact moment identities, Horner/block incidences, and positive lower/remainder pieces of the compact even determinant are checked; the original-coordinate full determinant incidence is the remaining proof bottleneck. Generated coefficients are not premises.

The remaining task is to prove that their assembled expression equals the required determinant in the original variables. Generated coefficient tables do not establish that identity or supply missing premises.

mapping.old: `[observed]` Actual physical rank-three determinant D1 stayed positive on the compact missing orbit interval with a large margin. Nearby seam scale alone does not force this: other initial scales fail later.

Nearby starting scales can fail later, so positivity is a property to establish for the actual source trajectory, not for every trajectory that starts near the same boundary.

mapping.old: `[proved/exact candidate]` Actual theta dynamics lie in a proved compact tube with `A>17`, controlled `−S`, and controlled `W`. Exact polynomial candidates are positive on the larger box `−1≤S≤0`, `A≥17`, `0≤W≤6/5`; finite-order closure does not imply an all-degree Xi producer.

Exact polynomial calculations suggest positivity on a larger rectangular region containing that enclosure. This separates two tasks: prove the source remains in the enclosure, then prove the determinant inequality there. Neither a finite-order enclosure nor a polynomial sign at this rank produces all-degree Xi positivity.

mapping.old: `[observed]` Direct D1 positivity is stronger and cleaner than projective-drift positivity on the physical cone. Scale variation is increasing/convex; clock-square variation is concave with positive third derivative. Alternating derivative hierarchy fails at fourth order.

These signs suggest a direct boundary-minimum proof. The alternating derivative pattern already fails at order four, so an all-orders complete-monotonicity argument is unavailable.

mapping.old: `[rejected]` Global wall monotonicity, upper-wall clock monotonicity, raw D1 monotonicity, simple factorization, and complete monotonicity are false or unavailable.

A localized geometric argument is needed; the finite determinant's observed positivity survives these failures.

mapping.old: `[observed]` After scale increase and clock concavity, D1 reduces to seam positivity plus one decreasing univariate outer face and its upper-corner value. This is the smallest surviving finite-gate architecture.
mapping.new: [Observation; proof target] The tested scale monotonicity and clock concavity reduce the reflected-theta determinant's minimum to its symmetry boundary and one outer one-variable boundary. That outer boundary was decreasing, leaving its endpoint as the final test. This is a candidate small collection of sufficient inequalities; the numerical reduction is not itself their analytic proof.

mapping.old: `[observed]` Projective drift is inward at the seam and positive away from it on tested boxes, but raw D1 is unimodal rather than monotone. Local nonzero projective jets alternate `+,-,+`, so absolute monotonicity is false.
mapping.new: [Observation] The projective motion associated with the reflected-theta determinant points inward at the symmetry boundary and had the desired sign on the tested interior boxes. The raw determinant nevertheless rises and then falls, and the first nonzero projective derivatives alternate +,−,+. Favorable inward motion must not be confused with monotonicity of the determinant or positivity of all derivatives.

mapping.old: `[proved]` Source dynamics contain an exact `sl₂` triple; physical scale differentiation is its Cartan derivative. This is the natural structure for a finite contravariant/Loewner proof.
mapping.new: [Reported analytic structure] The reflected-theta source dynamics admit three differential operators satisfying the sl₂ commutation relations; physical scale differentiation corresponds to the diagonal, or Cartan, operator. This supplies a concrete algebraic structure for studying finite matrix positivity. It does not by itself establish the required positive inner product or all-rank result.

mapping.old: `[rejected]` Raw coefficientwise matrix-Bernstein positivity fails although the assembled derivative matrix appears positive definite; cancellation between scale layers is essential.
mapping.new: [Rejected proof format] Testing each Bernstein coefficient of the reflected-theta derivative matrix for positivity fails, although the assembled matrix appears positive definite. Cancellation between different scale contributions is essential. A matrix or determinant argument may succeed where coefficient-by-coefficient signs cannot.

mapping.old: `[observed]` On the refined cone, all tested principal minors of the scale-velocity Hankel matrix are positive, selecting strict Loewner increase as a candidate mechanism.
mapping.new: [Observation] On the refined physical region, all tested principal minors of the Hankel matrix obtained by differentiating with respect to scale were positive. This suggests strict increase in the Loewner order, meaning that the matrix increment is positive definite. An analytic proof must establish that matrix inequality on the whole region.

mapping.old: `[rejected]` Full Bochner/positive-definite completion of the reflected theta fibre fails at six points. Positive definiteness survived all tested packets through five points. Thus use finite-order-5 or direct rank-three geometry, not an all-order measure representation.
mapping.new: [Rejected all-order extension] The reflected-theta kernel's proposed positive-definite completion fails for a six-point configuration. All tested configurations with at most five points passed. Consequently, a representation as the Fourier transform of a positive measure, which would imply positivity at every finite size, cannot serve this kernel as proposed. Finite-order or direct rank-three arguments remain separate possibilities.

mapping.new: [Reported finite certificate] For the restricted Weil quadratic form with the pole constraints imposed, rigorous finite numerical bounds establish positivity through logarithmic support length S=1, where aperture lambda=exp(S/2). Reported lower bounds for the least energy are approximately 0.518 at S=log(2) and 0.0014 at S=1. These certify the stated restricted range, not the unrestricted Weil positivity criterion for RH.

mapping.old: `[observed]` At aperture `λ=√2`, constrained ground energy is about `0.547`, versus unconstrained `1.33·10⁻³`. Resolved positivity persists to about `λ=2.1`; no sign-changing aperture appears up to `λ≈5`, but later Galerkin values are only upper bounds and decay super-exponentially.
mapping.new: [Observation] At aperture lambda=sqrt(2), imposing the pole constraints raises the computed least Weil energy from about 0.00133 to 0.547. Numerically resolved positivity persists to about lambda=2.1. No negative value was found up to roughly lambda=5, but the later finite-dimensional eigenvalues are only upper bounds on the true least energy and become extremely small; they cannot certify positivity there.

mapping.old: `[observed]` Archimedean-only constrained form becomes indefinite near `λ=1.8145`; each omitted prime power becomes decisive shortly after entering. Prime contributions have no fixed sign and must conspire collectively.
mapping.new: [Observation] Removing prime contributions from the pole-constrained Weil form makes it indefinite near aperture lambda=1.8145. Individual omitted prime powers become important shortly after their support thresholds are crossed. Prime contributions themselves have both signs. The arithmetic terms are essential collectively; adding primes cannot be justified as a sequence of positive corrections.

mapping.old: `[observed]` Both constrained and unconstrained ground-state Fourier zeros lock onto low zeta ordinates as aperture grows; pole directions accelerate locking but do not cause it. Extra interlacing zeros eventually appear from exponential-type counting.
mapping.new: [Observation] As the allowed support grows, Fourier-transform zeros of both constrained and unconstrained computed Weil ground states approach low zeta-zero ordinates. Pole constraints accelerate this alignment but are not its sole cause. Additional interlacing transform zeros eventually appear, so alignment of a few zeros is not a one-to-one global spectral identification.

mapping.old: `[observed]` Compact-Weil ground states lock one transform root to each low ordinate, but close pairs eventually merge while scalar ground energy barely changes. Pre-collapse root error scales approximately as separation `δ⁻³`; multiplicity control needs a Hermite/divided-difference channel.
mapping.new: [Observation] In computed compact-support Weil ground states, closely spaced transform zeros can merge even while the lowest energy barely changes. Before merging, the measured location error grows approximately as the inverse cube of the pair separation. A small scalar energy therefore does not ensure separate recovery of nearby zeros or their multiplicities; derivative samples or divided differences are needed to resolve a close pair.

mapping.old: `[proved]` Two point-sampling energies split exactly into average and antisymmetric channels; the antisymmetric channel vanishes quadratically at collision with limit controlled by the derivative norm.
mapping.new: [Reported analytic result] The combined squared sampling energy at two nearby points decomposes into the squared average response and the squared difference response. As the points merge, the difference channel vanishes quadratically and its rescaled limit measures a derivative norm. This identifies the additional observable needed when ordinary two-point sampling loses multiplicity information.

mapping.old: `[observed]` Ground autocorrelation monotonicity and post-first-atom cumulative prime–polar positivity survived finite Galerkin tests, while pointwise positivity of the completed error is false by known oscillation. Any proof must use ground-selected averaging of the sign-changing error.
mapping.new: [Observation] Computed Weil ground states had monotone autocorrelations and favorable cumulative prime/pole balances after the first contributing atom. The corresponding pointwise completed error changes sign. A proof using these observations must justify the averaging selected by the ground state; it cannot replace a signed oscillatory error by a pointwise positive function.

mapping.old: `[proved]` Published finite restricted-Weil matrices form an exact nested principal tower. Missing connector is convergence from those source matrices to the abstract Laurent/Galerkin compression.
mapping.new: [Reported analytic result; open limit] The published finite restricted-Weil matrices are nested principal submatrices of an exact matrix system. The missing result is convergence connecting these source-defined matrices with the proposed infinite-dimensional Laurent/Galerkin operator. Nestedness alone does not justify that identification or transfer finite positivity to the limit.

mapping.old: `[observed]` Fixed-pole parity energies stayed positive for `0<a≤8`; normalized margins oscillate around the sharp mass `2+γ−log(4π)≈0.04619`, with zero asymptotic margin. Any prime-side proof must reach that exact constant.
mapping.new: [Observation] The tested fixed-pole even/odd energy combinations were positive over their parameter range 0<a<=8. Their normalized margins oscillate around the exact mass 2+gamma−log(4*pi), approximately 0.04619, where gamma is Euler's constant, and the excess margin tends toward zero. A sharp prime-side argument must recover this constant; a uniformly loose positive allowance will not suffice.

mapping.old: `[observed]` Integer lags through `2·10⁷` remain far below the RH ceiling: maximum about 40% of it. Conditional recurrence to the ceiling is therefore extremely slow at accessible scales.
mapping.new: [Observation] The tested arithmetic lag function, evaluated at every integer lag through 20 million, reached only about 40% of the ceiling predicted under RH. This suggests that any conditional recurrence near that ceiling happens much later than accessible samples. Failure to approach the ceiling in this range is not evidence against the conditional recurrence theorem.

mapping.old: `[observed/proved]` Prime-truncated lag positive-definiteness fails a few hundredths past the first omitted prime-power lag. Under RH, continuum positive-definiteness pins every prime-power position and weight exactly: any nonzero single-kink perturbation creates negative high-frequency directions.
mapping.new: [Observation; conditional analytic obstruction] Truncating prime-power terms in the arithmetic lag kernel causes finite positive-definiteness tests to fail shortly after the first omitted prime-power lag. Separately, an analytic result conditional on RH says that continuum positive definiteness fixes every prime-power location and weight exactly: any nonzero perturbation of one such corner creates a negative high-frequency direction. This conditional rigidity result is not an unconditional proof of RH.

mapping.old: `[observed]` Arithmetic Gram least eigenvalues scale approximately `c/N`, `c≈0.09–0.10`; top eigenvalues scale as `N/(1/4+γ_j²)`. Finite PSD tests are insensitive to sufficiently high off-line zeros until matrix size is roughly square-root in zero height.
mapping.new: [Observation] In the tested arithmetic Gram matrices of size N, the smallest eigenvalue behaves approximately as c/N with c around 0.09–0.10; leading eigenvalues follow the tested zeta-ordinate scales N/(1/4+gamma_j²). Here gamma_j is the imaginary part of the j-th sampled critical-line zero. Finite positive-semidefinite tests can miss sufficiently high hypothetical off-line zeros until the matrix is much larger; positive small matrices are weak evidence about the full zero set.

mapping.old: `[observed]` Full infinite-lattice HCF receiver capacity improves the three-center threshold only from about `0.3437` to `0.3821`; receiver optimization is not the active bottleneck.
mapping.new: [Observation] For the Hedenmalm critical feature 2/(1+(z−t)²), extending the receiver from three sampling centers to a complete integer lattice improves the measured capacity threshold only from about 0.3437 to 0.3821. This modest gain does not produce the missing arithmetic source covariance. Further optimization of the same scalar receiver is unlikely to address the main source-identification obstacle.

mapping.old: `[rejected]` Scalar signed separator mixtures suppress off-diagonal response only outside a collision radius, with coefficient norm and negative lobe exploding as radius shrinks. Uniform HCF needs matrix/source cancellation or zero spacing.
mapping.new: [Rejected mechanism] Signed mixtures of scalar separating kernels suppress cross responses only when spectral points remain outside a minimum separation. As that separation shrinks, the coefficient norm and the adverse negative lobe grow rapidly. Such mixtures are not uniform close-pair controls without an additional spacing theorem or a matrix/source cancellation mechanism.

mapping.old: `[rejected]` Fixed-degree gamma-cell factors add only `O(T)` mobile off-line zeros versus zeta's `T log T`; they are finite-height falsifiers, not asymptotic density obstructions. Genuine adversaries need `N(T)`-scale mobility.
mapping.new: [Rejected asymptotic inference] Multiplying by a fixed-degree admissible gamma-cell factor can introduce moving off-line zeros, but only in number proportional to height T. Zeta has on the order of T log(T) zeros. These factors can falsify finite-height structural claims; they cannot alone force a positive asymptotic proportion of off-line zeros. A density obstruction needs a perturbation affecting comparably many zeros.

mapping.old: `[rejected/observed]` Even positive strictly log-concave kernels can have negative rank-three packets; FE-symmetrized atoms can have off-axis zeros; finite causal/symmetric Volterra truncations were indefinite. Classical Laguerre wall jets `L₁,L₂` stayed positive, but close-pair failure is invisible to pointwise wall jets.
mapping.new: [Rejected sufficiency claims; finite observations] Positive, strictly log-concave kernels can still have a negative rank-three test. Enforcing functional-equation symmetry on source atoms does not prevent off-axis zeros, and tested finite causal symmetric Volterra operators were indefinite. Conversely, the first two pointwise Laguerre derivative tests can remain positive while close-pair control fails. mapping.old: `[observed]` Multi-band isolated-zero ladders did not hide energy materially better than one chirped band; this does not prove the full isolation law.
mapping.new: [Observation] In tests of observables designed to isolate a zero, combining several frequency bands did not conceal substantially more energy than one band with a varying phase frequency. This gives no observed advantage to that particular extra complexity. It is not a uniform lower bound for all possible isolated-zero constructions.

mapping.old: `[proved/observed]` Uniform damping gives an `n`-uniform exponential floor; data suggest a sharper scale polynomial in `K/g` for `K≲g`. Gram/Ingham bounds alone do not resolve wide real-part spreads.

This follows by comparison with the undamped integral. Finite tests of unequal decay rates did not violate the proposed analogous floor, but do not prove it. A stronger polynomial-scale lower bound when decay rates are small compared with the frequency gap remains conjectural. Do not extrapolate an initial decrease with n into a contradiction of the proved uniform-decay floor.

mapping.old: `[proved]` True finite Euler-product log determinant has a second-order expansion with explicit cubic remainder. Current bound uses an entrywise norm that is too large; an `n`-uniform operator-norm refinement is missing.

mapping.old: Finite-prime analysis must assemble Euler product first and organize around pairwise log-ratio beats; fixed Euler jets or independent one-prime boundary layers are not valid building blocks.

mapping.old: `[observed]` Diagonal dominance `S²≤Q` survived every cutoff through `2,097,152`; `[proved]` diagonal energy has exact update law and unconditional bound `Q(M)≤722M²`. The required nonpositive total off-diagonal sign remains open.

mapping.old: `[rejected/proved]` Every-step energy contraction fails already at `M=5`; every-order nonincreasing paths fail at `M=7`. A local increase can still remain below the original diagonal, so contraction and ceiling are distinct.

mapping.old: `[observed]` Original-diagonal ceiling survived finite exhaustive path searches through 32, greedy paths through 1024, fixed-late policies through 32768, and joint-prime policies through 8192. None gives all-cutoff control.

mapping.new: [Observation] On complete processed-prime subset state spaces through cutoff 32, the tested low-energy successor, negative-support and two-step repair rules found admissible continuations. mapping.old: `[rejected]` Homogeneous descent of the geometric certificate, logarithmically averaged successor slack, uniform averaging of successor envelopes, and pointwise prime-2 envelope monotonicity all fail. Successful selection must retain prime-specific signed interactions.

mapping.old: `[rejected/proved]` Simultaneously requiring nonempty-energy dissipation and envelope admission has a unique reachable trap at `M=25`; head-square release pays forced transverse growth. Generic sharp next-step bound is `V_next≤3V/2`.
mapping.new: [Reported obstruction and bound] At cutoff 25, the rule demanding both dissipation of all nonempty-group energy and admission by the proposed successor bound has a reachable trapped state. Releasing energy from the distinguished head group can pay the necessary growth elsewhere. A general sharp one-step bound allows the tracked energy to grow by a factor 3/2; demanding contraction excludes a necessary mechanism.

mapping.old: `[rejected/proved]` Keeping every nonempty fibre nonnegative fails from `M=21`; at least one moving defect is necessary. Exact defect-triangle and mixed-transverse compensation results capture the positive survivor.
mapping.new: [Reported obstruction] Keeping every nonempty group of divisor-source terms nonnegative fails from cutoff 21. At least one group must be allowed to carry a moving negative contribution. Derived triangle and mixed-group compensation identities describe how such a contribution can be balanced; universal positivity of each group is the wrong target.

mapping.old: `[observed]` A fixed potential `V+αH²` admits complete monotone paths through 32 for `0≤α≲0.201`, but no fixed `α` gives a good next move from every state. Path existence is weaker than local extendability.
mapping.new: [Observation; rejected universal policy] A potential equal to remaining-group energy plus alpha times the squared signed head admitted complete decreasing paths through cutoff 32 for 0<=alpha approximately <=0.201. No single fixed alpha guarantees an acceptable next step from every state. Existence of a successful complete path is therefore weaker than a universal greedy rule based on this scalar potential.

mapping.old: `[rejected]` Binary gcd packets and individual exact-gcd groups need not be nonpositive. Compensation crosses distinct gcd classes.
mapping.new: [Rejected termwise sign] Neither binary greatest-common-divisor packets nor individual exact-greatest-common-divisor groups of the source cross terms need be nonpositive. Favorable cancellation can occur between different greatest-common-divisor classes. Proving a sign for each class separately would impose a false requirement.

mapping.old: `[rejected]` Positive exact-gcd mass is not bounded by diagonal with constant one; complete signed cross sums nevertheless remained negative at all tested cutoffs. Preserve `S²=D+P−N` and bound `P−N`, not `P` alone.
mapping.new: [Rejected bound; surviving target] The total positive contribution from exact-greatest-common-divisor groups can exceed the diagonal energy. Writing total-sum squared as diagonal + positive cross mass − negative cross mass shows the useful target: bound the difference of the two cross masses, not the positive mass alone.

mapping.old: `[observed]` One-prime adjacency flow compensated positive gcd mass at tested cutoffs, but shared negative-neighbor capacity, not isolated vertices, controls the residual. Möbius parity-class balance alone is insufficient because graph neighborhoods restrict access.
mapping.new: [Observation] A flow along edges corresponding to one-prime changes compensated the positive greatest-common-divisor mass in the tested source graphs. The limiting issue is shared capacity: several positive groups may need the same negative neighbors. Balancing total Möbius parity classes ignores that access constraint; a uniform proof would need an appropriate neighborhood or transport-capacity estimate.

mapping.old: `[rejected]` Coarea mass-envelope greedy paths, coupled-sector steepest paths, and the proposed unit transverse budget fail at growing cutoffs. Local pair variance or average cancellation does not prevent coherent amplification.
mapping.new: [Rejected selection rules] Greedy rules based on averaged mass allowances, simultaneous steepest descent of coupled groups, and a fixed unit allowance for transverse energy fail as cutoffs grow. Small local variance or average cancellation does not prevent many signed terms from amplifying coherently. A successful rule must control that collective effect.

mapping.old: `[rejected/proved]` Advancing retained prime front can increase transverse energy even with small receiving coordinates. Child-inactive helper blocks commute exactly with later transverse costs, so head balancing cannot change the sign of those gains; a cumulative budget is required.
mapping.new: [Reported obstruction and identity] Processing an additional retained prime can increase energy in the remaining groups even when the receiving coordinates are small. Helper groups that are inactive in the copied child commute with later transverse costs, so adjusting the head through those helpers cannot reverse the gain. The replacement target is a cumulative signed budget, not independent repairs of every step.

mapping.old: `[rejected/proved]` Increasing middle-prime order exceeds original diagonal even after all fixed scalar reserves are removed. Analytic nested child-head amplification defeats every fixed quadratic ceiling uniformly over fixed scalar-reserve choices; adaptive orders remain open.
mapping.new: [Reported obstruction] Processing middle primes in increasing order can exceed the original divisor-source diagonal budget even after the tested fixed scalar reserves are included. A derived nested amplification mechanism defeats every fixed quadratic ceiling in that class of reserve choices. Adaptive prime orders are not ruled out; the obstruction concerns the specified fixed-order and fixed-reserve mechanism.

mapping.old: `[observed]` Fixed small cores contain many asymptotically energy-increasing edges, including parents still far below original budget. This points to signed dilation correlation rather than local reserve.
mapping.new: [Observation] Fixed small prime cores contain many transitions whose asymptotic energy change is positive, including transitions starting far below the original budget. Thus distance below the budget does not itself predict the next sign. Signed correlations under dilation are a more informative quantity to investigate than local scalar reserve alone.

mapping.old: `[observed/proved]` Joint two-prime selection exposes a real middle/late amplitude window: both first moves may increase while their common endpoint compensates. Exact continuous optimum is classified; existence of an unused prime in the needed window at every stage is open.
mapping.new: [Observation; reported optimization] Two primes chosen jointly can repair a state even when either first move increases energy. The corresponding continuous amplitude optimization has an exact classification, exposing an interval of useful middle/late amplitudes. It remains open whether an unused actual prime lies in the required interval at every stage; continuous feasibility does not establish arithmetic availability.

mapping.old: `[observed]` Coupled head/prime-2 source profiles admit positive zero-sum circuits; a `2,11,15` circuit also removes inherited prime-2 debt. Uniform capacity and complete exhaustion remain open.
mapping.new: [Observation] Coupled signed-head and prime-2 profiles admit tested positive combinations whose net unwanted contribution is zero. A combination indexed by 2,11,15 also cancels the inherited prime-2 debt. These examples motivate cancellation circuits, but neither uniform available capacity nor an exhaustion procedure covering the complete source has been proved.

mapping.old: `[rejected]` Independent Bernoulli half-selection eventually has mean-head square above original diagonal; zeta-pole analysis gives the analytic obstruction.

The analytic explanation uses zeta-pole behavior. Independent random selection therefore cannot establish the proposed bound merely by averaging; any successful probabilistic selection needs additional dependence or arithmetic structure.

mapping.old: `[proved]` Literal unsigned channel orientation and square-root lower bound hold independently of the finite positive scans.
mapping.new: [Reported analytic result] For the literal divisor source, the unsigned comparison channel has the required orientation and a square-root lower bound independently of the finite sign scans. This provides one controlled part of the construction. It does not establish the unresolved sign of the complete signed off-diagonal energy.

mapping.old: `[rejected]` Ordinary decreasing weights, prefix-by-prefix positive pairings, and geometric/Laplace component positivity do not prove the source bound. Exact Abel representation as a mixture of prefix channels survives.
mapping.new: [Rejected positivity shortcut; analytic survivor] Ordinary decreasing weights, positivity at every prefix and positivity of separate geometric/Laplace components do not prove the signed divisor-source bound. An exact Abel summation formula still expresses the weighted quantity using prefix channels. That representation can organize a proof, but its components cannot all be assigned the favorable sign.

mapping.old: `[rejected]` Blockwise feedback, uniform merge contraction, pointwise block contraction, and a fixed average decrement across scales fail. Literal source has aggregate cancellation plus locally coherent deficit clusters; no dependency-closed positive salvage was found.
mapping.new: [Rejected local-feedback mechanisms] Uniform contraction under merging, pointwise contraction of each block and a fixed average energy decrement across scales fail for the literal divisor source. The data contain aggregate cancellation alongside locally coherent clusters of adverse terms. No dependency-closed positive replacement theorem emerged from these particular feedback attempts; they do not refute other cumulative arithmetic bounds.

mapping.old: `[observed]` Complete reciprocal flux was positive for every cutoff `2≤N≤512`, but positivity alone gives no subpower upper bound.

mapping.old: `[rejected]` Absolute row variation is not always within four times flux, and the Bernoulli mean profile can miss nearly all row variation. Complete finite head, nonzero Fourier modes, and outer Möbius signs must remain.

mapping.old: `[observed]` Exact-gcd total variation stayed below four diagonal units in tested raw/tapered sources. Individual groups have both signs; complete-gcd estimates remain plausible, not proved.
mapping.new: [Observation] After grouping complete reciprocal-divisor covariance terms by their exact greatest common divisor, the tested total variation stayed below four times the diagonal comparison quantity for both raw and tapered sources. Individual groups take both signs. The observation supports investigating a bound on the complete grouping; it does not prove the constant four uniformly.

mapping.old: `[rejected]` Separately charging head polynomial and corrected remainder can exceed the same budget even when the signed head/tail budget passes. Retain each head as one signed object.

Existing bounds on omitted tails are also too large to justify full transfer. Averaging has a measured finite benefit, but the proposed quantitative estimate is not supported.

mapping.old: `[rejected]` Choosing cutoffs by minimum harmonic head does not suppress complementary tail: roughly half or more lies in the first block. Exact first-tail source is `nH_N+M(n)−M(N)`.

The exact first-tail expression contains both the harmonic partial sum and the difference of Mertens sums. Minimizing only the harmonic term ignores a leading arithmetic contribution.

mapping.old: `[rejected]` Minimizing the all-gcd head polynomial does not consistently minimize full residue energy; the linear unit-source cross term changes finite rankings. Formal all-gcd subpower remainder remains valid but does not control complete tail.

The linear cross term with the unit source can change which finite cutoff is best. A derived subpower bound for the corrected remainder does not automatically control this full energy or its tail.

mapping.old: `[observed]` Bounded coefficient repair can reduce finite heat residuals by many orders. Adjusting nonsquarefree coefficients and coordinating the initial and tail portions both help; nearly optimal finite errors remain possible even when the first quarter of coefficients is fixed to Möbius values. These are finite approximations, not constructions with proved error tending to zero as the fixed prefix grows.

mapping.old: `[observed/proved]` Positive averages of raw Möbius cutoffs reach small finite errors while preserving Möbius signs. Successful near-identity power damping cannot have `ε_N log N→0`; mass must move cofinally away from terminal cutoff.

For near-identity power damping with exponent epsilon_N at cutoff N, the successful asymptotic mechanism cannot have epsilon_N*log(N) tending to zero: averaging weight must move sufficiently far from the terminal cutoff. Finite small errors alone do not meet that necessary escape condition.

mapping.old: `[observed]` Freezing a growing prefix has a visible cost under monotone positive averaging, largely removed by allowing a nonmonotone sign-preserving envelope. Remaining task is actual residual control as frozen prefix grows.
mapping.new: [Observation] Fixing a growing initial segment of Möbius coefficients increases error when the remaining positive averaging weights must be monotone. Allowing a nonmonotone envelope while preserving coefficient signs removes much of the measured cost. The unresolved issue is convergence of the actual approximation error as the fixed segment grows; relaxed finite fitting is not that convergence proof.

mapping.old: `[observed]` Enforcing more exact boundary moments is not monotonically beneficial; error is concentrated outside Taylor-scale neighborhood. Local derivatives and harmonic charge do not settle global residual.
mapping.new: [Observation] Imposing more exact boundary moments does not monotonically improve the tested arithmetic approximation. Much of the error lies outside the neighborhood described by the matched Taylor derivatives. Matching local derivatives and a harmonic charge therefore does not control the global residual; the missing observable must measure the region where the error remains.

mapping.old: `[rejected/observed]` Recovery-gap positive-moment model has a degree-17 square witness with negative numerical functional; finite Hausdorff differences can all pass while Hankel positivity fails. Global log-convexity remains open.
mapping.new: [Numerical obstruction candidate] Define recovery gaps delta_(m−1) by minimizing max W(r)^m*abs(R(r)) on 0<=r<=1/4 over polynomials R of degree at most m whose coefficient of r^(m−1) equals one, with W(r)=1−sqrt(1−4*r). For gamma_k=(delta_k/delta_0)^2, a canonical degree-17 squared-polynomial functional is numerically negative, stable under independent 140/230-digit computations. All 2080 tested Hausdorff finite differences nevertheless pass. Thus those finite differences do not establish a positive representing measure; an exact negative-square proof remains open. This does not refute the weaker log-convexity question delta_(k+1)^2<=delta_k*delta_(k+2).

mapping.old: `[proved]` Recovery multiplier has uniform block growth and exact closed spectral disc of radius `ρ≈0.0173600`, independent of moment positivity.

A paper argument proves uniform block growth and identifies its spectrum as the closed disc of radius rho≈0.01736004210, the exponential decay rate of delta_k. The argument does not assume that the squared gaps form a positive moment sequence. This operator result survives the numerical obstruction to that stronger moment interpretation; the paper dependencies and operator result have not been fully formalized.

mapping.old: `[rejected/proved]` Normalized chord-basis bound fails from three chords. Exact `27D+R` optimum is known; `27D−R` has signed capacity `28/27` versus monotone capacity `1`, proving genuine reversal advantage.
mapping.new: [Reported exact counterexample and optimum] For products of chord increments along a path with total variation one, the sum of responses normalized by individual chord capacities can exceed one starting at three chords. With D the three adjacent disjoint chords and R the three nested chords on six ordered endpoints, the combination 27D−R has maximum absolute response 1 for monotone paths but 28/27 when reversals are allowed. Thus path reversal has a genuine advantage that monotone-only optimization misses. The related positive combination 27D+R also has an exactly derived optimum.

mapping.old: `[proved]` Cubic reversal enclosure depth is exactly one. No finite search found a higher-degree counterexample to analogous shallow stabilization; this remains open outside proved cubic class.
mapping.new: [Reported finite-degree result; open extension] In the cubic chord-response class, one level of the reversal-enclosure construction suffices exactly. Finite searches found no counterexample to analogous shallow stabilization at higher degree. That extension remains conjectural; a proved cubic closure cannot be assumed for arbitrary numbers of chords.

mapping.old: `[rejected/proved]` Real projected minimum balance admits off-line nonzeros of zeta and therefore is not a sufficient zero/location test. Retain the missing imaginary constraint or another independent equation.
mapping.new: [Reported counterexample] Keeping only the real part of the proposed arithmetic minimum-balance condition admits complex points off the critical line where zeta is nonzero. The real projected condition is therefore neither a sufficient zero test nor a sufficient location test. A surviving formulation needs the missing imaginary equation or another independent condition.

mapping.old: `[proved]` Every critical-line zero has a finite arithmetic value below the explicit tail boundary; observed minimizing moduli vary across primes/composites and Möbius signs. Finite minimum labels do not determine zero location.
mapping.new: [Reported analytic result; observation] At every critical-line zero, the arithmetic minimization quantity attains a finite value below its explicit tail bound. Computed minimizing indices include primes and composites with different Möbius signs. The label of the minimizing index therefore does not determine the zero's horizontal location; finite attainment and zero selection are different questions.

mapping.old: `[rejected]` Individual divisor terms are not monotone/dominant; large finite excursions coexist with proved power-decay envelopes.
mapping.new: [Rejected termwise argument] Individual divisor terms in the arithmetic phase/minimum construction are neither monotone nor uniformly dominant. Large finite excursions coexist with derived power-decay bounds for the complete remainder. A proof must account for cancellation or envelopes of the assembled expression rather than extrapolate a single term's behavior.

mapping.old: `[rejected]` Prime-sieve phase sign and monotone-insertion laws fail. A sufficiently late negative imaginary tail survives analytically, but supplies no sign for the full unit-head limit.
mapping.new: [Rejected sign law; analytic survivor] Inserting primes into the phase construction does not preserve the proposed sign or monotonicity. A sufficiently late imaginary tail does have a derived negative sign, but that does not determine the sign after adding the initial unit contribution and all earlier terms. Tail sign is not a sign theorem for the complete limit.

mapping.old: `[observed]` Proposed successor cutoff `t<2πn` survived the finite ordinary-remainder scan. Cellwise negativity is false at special heights, so any proof must use cancellation across cells.
mapping.new: [Observation] The proposed relation between spectral height t and successor cutoff n, namely t<2*pi*n, survived the finite ordinary-remainder tests. Negativity of every individual cell fails at special heights. Any proof using this cutoff relation must establish cancellation across cells, not replace the sum by a false cellwise sign.

mapping.old: `[rejected/proved]` Individual logarithmic phase turns may be positive while all tested cumulative prefixes are negative. Constant-speed prefix nonpositivity is proved; logarithmic clock transfer remains open.
mapping.new: [Reported constant-clock result; open transfer] Individual increments of a logarithmically parametrized arithmetic phase can be positive even when all tested cumulative prefixes are negative. Prefix nonpositivity has an analytic proof for the related constant-speed clock. Transferring that result to the actual logarithmic clock remains open; reparametrization does not preserve the needed signs automatically.

mapping.new: [Rejected clock invariance] The favorable phase signs from a constant-speed clock fail under arbitrary exponential acceleration. Restricted clock layers survived the finite tests, but this does not justify unrestricted clock changes. Any time-change argument must state and prove the conditions preserving the cumulative sign.

mapping.old: `[rejected]` Growing-modulus remainder is not bounded after the naive main subtraction; it contains a universal `−(1/2)log p` term plus explicit real power and complex correction terms, not zero-specific cancellation.

These contributions are not specific to zeta zeros. They must be removed or retained explicitly before claiming a zero-dependent cancellation.

mapping.old: `[rejected]` Mixed refinement correction neither vanishes at zeros nor lies in tested scalar/two-coordinate repair spaces. Exact finite correction cocycle survives.
mapping.new: [Rejected repair space; analytic identity] The mixed correction created by arithmetic refinement does not vanish at zeta zeros and is not captured by the tested scalar or two-coordinate repairs. An exact finite composition identity for the correction survives. That identity is useful bookkeeping, but it does not collapse the correction to a zero or to the proposed low-dimensional repair.

mapping.old: `[rejected/proved]` Complete multiplicativity does not force finite endpoint-to-curvature sign: exact positive and negative tangent directions exist via paired primes.
mapping.new: [Reported counterexamples] Complete multiplicativity of the source coefficients does not fix the sign relating finite endpoint data to curvature. Paired-prime constructions give exact tangent directions of both signs. A curvature-selection argument needs additional arithmetic compatibility beyond complete multiplicativity.

mapping.old: `[rejected]` Mixed chronological area is not rank at most two at tested zeros; endpoint area identities do not collapse contributions from many time pairs.
mapping.new: [Numerical rejection] At tested zeta zeros, the mixed area recording interactions between different times has rank greater than two. Identities involving only endpoint areas do not eliminate those many-time contributions. A two-dimensional endpoint model therefore omits information present in the chronological source.
